findings.title: A successful edit replay can permanently skip the alert
findings.body: If a No-to-Yes update commits but execution stops before after() is registered, the retry loads Yes as `stored`. The write helper recognizes a successful replay, but this condition is now false, so no email is ever attempted. Fault injection using the actual action body with mocked dependencies reproduced a committed Yes followed by a successful replay with zero scheduled callbacks. The create path explicitly handles this recovery case; the edit path does not.
findings.recommendation: Persist alert intent atomically with the No-to-Yes update and resume unattempted intent on replay. Keep claimed attempts deduplicated to preserve the no-retry policy for failed sends.

findings.title: Pending status never updates when background delivery fails
findings.body: The redirected inspection page computes alert status once on the server. If it renders while the alert is sending, a later failure leaves 'The alert email is being sent' displayed indefinitely. The five-minute stale warning also requires another render; no polling, subscription, or refresh timer exists. Because failed sends are deliberately not retried, this conceals the instruction to call the contact—the design's recovery mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Refresh pending alert status until it reaches a terminal state, and trigger the stale warning without requiring a manual reload. Handle the initial pre-claim state as pending during that window.

storedJob.rendered:
# Codex Adversarial Review

Target: branch diff against master
Verdict: needs-attention

Do not ship yet: interrupted edits can lose alerts, and the status page can hide subsequent failures. Reviewed the exact GitHub diff against master; local Git and test execution were unavailable.

Findings:
- [high] A successful edit replay can permanently skip the alert (src/app/dashboard/projects/[id]/forms/working-in-waterways/actions.ts:158-160)
  If a No-to-Yes update commits but execution stops before after() is registered, the retry loads Yes as `stored`. The write helper recognizes a successful replay, but this condition is now false, so no email is ever attempted. Fault injection using the actual action body with mocked dependencies reproduced a committed Yes followed by a successful replay with zero scheduled callbacks. The create path explicitly handles this recovery case; the edit path does not.
  Recommendation: Persist alert intent atomically with the No-to-Yes update and resume unattempted intent on replay. Keep claimed attempts deduplicated to preserve the no-retry policy for failed sends.
- [medium] Pending status never updates when background delivery fails (src/app/dashboard/projects/[id]/forms/working-in-waterways/[submissionId]/page.tsx:68-73)
  The redirected inspection page computes alert status once on the server. If it renders while the alert is sending, a later failure leaves 'The alert email is being sent' displayed indefinitely. The five-minute stale warning also requires another render; no polling, subscription, or refresh timer exists. Because failed sends are deliberately not retried, this conceals the instruction to call the contact—the design's recovery mechanism.
  Recommendation: Refresh pending alert status until it reaches a terminal state, and trigger the stale warning without requiring a manual reload. Handle the initial pre-claim state as pending during that window.

Next steps:
- Add an action-level regression covering interruption after the edit commits, followed by replay.
- Verify delayed failure and abandoned sending states become visible on an already-open inspection page.
